obligations.note: purge_due skips a closed payee only when legal_hold is set and category is not employee, so employee payees on legal hold are purged after the retention cutoff. RET-1 requires NPI never be purged while a legal hold applies, and no approved exception covers RET-1 or payments.retention. The registered control test is only sample coverage and still passes, so it does not show the hold rule for every payee.
CHG-25108 is approved by change manager Grace Kim before review and lists payments.retention, the component assigned to the only touched path, apps/baseline-payments/payments/retention.py.
Mara Costa, a payments change_approver and not the author Linh Nguyen, gave a code_review approval.
That approval names head commit a2e976b95dc05e5c3735b3498d201f1e7901f528, and the change has no later commits.

records/ci/run.json records a successful payments suite on the head commit, and the JUnit digest shows 172 tests, 0 failures, and 0 skipped, including the registered RET-1 test test_sampled_purge_respects_hold.
retention.py is mapped to payments.retention with security_sensitive false, so a security_review approval is not required.
The only changed path is application code, not a protected controls, control-test, or CI path, so a control_owner approval is not required.
The ticket type is standard and the change is not marked emergency, so a post-implementation review is not due.
The register has no approved, unexpired exception scoped to RET-1 and payments.retention, and this change does not rely on the other exceptions (expired SES-1, mortgage LOG-1, or withdrawn MFA-1).
The diff does not change any path covered by the acceptance ledger, so prior evidence for those other obligations has not lapsed. RET-1 has no ledger entry and is judged from the new retention code.

summary: The change alters payments retention so a legal hold stops purge only when the payee is not an employee. Employee payees past the closed-account retention period are still purged while a legal hold applies, which violates RET-1, and nothing in the exception register excuses it. Change-ticket, independent approval, commit coverage, CI, and the other process gates are in order, but a single product violation blocks acceptance.
